chapter: Instruments, tenors and the current band
title: Tom Scott as co-producer and the lyricon
summary: Tom Scott brought a lyricon for Herman, who handed it back to him; Scott played it on the tracks and co-produced the album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah. It's like a triangle, as a matter of fact. And then your last one was -- was Gary involved in one of them?
Gary did one, and a young man whom I've
known casually for years, an alto saxophonist out here, (unintelligible), and he's very good.
You had Tom Scott on this one.
He was there. He was co-co-co-coproducer.
He walked in to bring me -- this is a beautiful story, I think. He walked in to bring one of his two -- what is that instrument called?

Lyricanz, and he brought one for me to try and show me how to finger it and the whole thing, because I might dig, like, blowing on it. And I realized that it might be a lot of fun, after testing for about a half a second, but I also realized that it would take a great deal of time for me to begin to cope with it. So I said -- I asked him to go into the booth and take over. And when the whole -- we had done our part of the tapes, for him to come in and then play the lyric wherever it was necessary and where it should be.
But he is in there really as a co-producer.
Very interesting. So, again, the spirit of --

And he came out and helped us put the charts tracks together. He was a very together guy. And once again, it goes back to the very beginnings of all jazz music. Let's not make that -- play down that part because it's very important that young men today, coming up, and who are into where it's all at, to still have this gay feeling of abandon, let's put it together and have a ball, right?
